# Presentations

Establish the audience's decision and whether the deck is presented live, read alone or both. Ask only when this materially changes the requested work and cannot be inferred. Preserve the requested slide count, approved order and editing scope.

Assess the argument across the whole deck before polishing slides. Each slide should contribute a clear point; do not force every slide into the same layout or heading syntax. Fit the evidence and explanation to the reader's knowledge and the medium's space constraints.

For live talks, let the slide carry the point and visible evidence, with spoken detail in notes. For read-alone decks, include enough explanation to interpret the evidence and recommendation without a presenter. Never hide material qualifications only in notes.

Label comparison subjects, dates/versions, units, scales, sources and consequential conditions. Distinguish measured outcomes, lab scores, targets and assumptions. Do not convert a prototype comparison into an incumbent-versus-new claim or infer commercial returns from design scores.

Use Sales Pitch Reviewer for customer-facing commercial reasoning; do not apply a sales narrative to an internal technical review. Use the presentation authoring skill for files and render inspection. An outline review does not establish slide readability or visual quality.
